leads.summary: Restore the executable bit on bin/omarchy-system-logout (and on the changed test file)
leads.location: bin/omarchy-system-logout, file mode 100755 -> 100644 in 0056062e; test/shell.d/system-power-test.sh also 100755 -> 100644
leads.consequence: A source checkout cannot execute the logout command. The menu's bare command and the dev-linked PATH can instead resolve the older packaged /usr/bin copy, so a developer may silently test the old implementation; without that fallback the action is not found. The test runner discovers the new test with bash, but the positive logout case fails Permission denied, which makes test/shell and test/all fail, and the executable-only CLI metadata scan skips the command. The shipped omarchy PKGBUILD uses install -Dm755, so this is a checkout, CI and dev-link regression rather than a claim that the installed package lacks execution permission. Restore both tracked 100755 modes.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (N1); corroborated; also confirmed by coordinator via GitHub tree API

leads.summary: Clean merge with open #11151 makes the shared power test fail on logout's legitimate single scheduling attempt
leads.location: test/shell.d/system-power-test.sh:73-82, combined with #11151's negative-control check at merged/result-11151.sh:80-93
leads.consequence: PR #11151 adds a user-bus to system-bus fallback to reboot and shutdown, so its negative-control test expects two systemd-run calls. This PR extends that test loop to logout, which has only the single --user scheduling call. The test files merge without conflict, but the combined test fails after the two reboot/shutdown cases, even with this PR's executable-mode bug fixed. If both PRs merge, adjust the expected negative call count by action or split logout's single-attempt assertion into its own case; otherwise the shell suite stays red.
leads.triage: factual; coordinator verified via #11151 diff and independent git merge-file (identical to Sol's merged file); Opus confirmed in sandboxed run2 M2/M3 during self-check

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up to the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12254#issuecomment-5834536402) and the [author reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12254#issuecomment-5842689422), checked at `0056062e`.

**Outcome:** `0056062e` addresses the earlier points in content. The same commit removes the executable bit from `bin/omarchy-system-logout`, so the PR's own power test now fails on a clean checkout and `omarchy logout` no longer resolves from a checkout. GitHub also still links #12233 as an issue this PR closes.

| Earlier point | Status at `0056062e` |
|---|---|
| Logout scheduling matches reboot and shutdown and aborts before the OSD and window closing on failure | Still holds; the script's only content change is the comment |
| Repository test passes on the head | No longer holds as committed (mode change below); passes with the mode restored |
| "Fixes #12233" not demonstrated for the menu path | Resolved in the description; GitHub still links the issue (below) |
| Second code-comment sentence described removed code | Resolved; the comment now matches reboot and shutdown |
| Optional test improvement: stub `uwsm`, `systemctl`, `omarchy-osd` | Resolved |

**Verified:** In an isolated sandbox, every backend the power test could reach (`systemd-run`, `uwsm`, `systemctl`, `omarchy-osd`, `omarchy-state`, `omarchy-hyprland-window-close-all`, `sleep`) resolves to the test's own stubs, and the expected logs now assert that the OSD follows scheduling. With the logout mode restored, the test passes and still fails against the base logout script, a copy without `|| exit 1`, and a copy that shows the OSD before scheduling.

### `bin/omarchy-system-logout` is no longer executable

`0056062e` changes both files from `100755` to `100644`. The test file's mode does not matter (`test/shell` runs it with `bash`), but the logout script is executed directly:

```text
                                  9c497363                   0056062e
bin/omarchy-system-logout mode    100755                     100644
system-power-test.sh logout case  ok                         Permission denied, then not ok
omarchy logout --help             prints help                exit 127, Unknown Omarchy command
omarchy system --help             lists logout               no logout entry
```

The `quattro` tip matches `9c497363` on the mode and both dispatcher rows (its test has no logout case). `bin/omarchy` only considers files that pass `-x` (`load_commands`, `resolve_direct_route`). In the sandbox, restoring only the mode on otherwise identical content makes the test and the dispatcher cases pass again, on the head and on a trial merge into the `quattro` tip.

**Impact:** `./test/shell` reports `system-power-test.sh` as failed. On a dev-linked checkout, where `$OMARCHY_PATH/bin` comes first on `PATH`, `omarchy logout` and `omarchy system logout` fail as shown. From source and bash command lookup (not tested in a live session), Menu > System > Logout would skip the checkout copy and run a packaged `/usr/bin/omarchy-system-logout` if one is installed (in current packages, the older `nohup` version), or fail otherwise. Packaged installs are not affected: the omarchy PKGBUILDs install `bin/*` with `install -Dm755`.

**Suggested change:** Run `git update-index --chmod=+x bin/omarchy-system-logout test/shell.d/system-power-test.sh` and commit. `git ls-tree HEAD bin/omarchy-system-logout` should then show `100755`.

### #12233 is still linked as closed by this PR

The PR's `closingIssuesReferences` currently lists #12233, so GitHub still treats it as an issue this PR closes. The rewritten description says "...so it does not close #12233", and "close #12233" matches GitHub's closing-keyword syntax, which does not account for the "not". A link left over from the original "Fixes #12233" is also possible.

**Impact:** Merging into `quattro`, the default branch, would likely close #12233 while the menu logout failure remains unexplained, which is the outcome the earlier review pointed to.

**Suggested change:** Reword without a closing keyword directly before the reference, for example "#12233 should stay open until the menu path is confirmed", then check that the Development sidebar no longer lists #12233. If it still does, unlink it there.

**Related open PRs:** #11151 changes the same failure loop in `test/shell.d/system-power-test.sh` to expect two `systemd-run` attempts (user manager, then a system-manager fallback), which fits reboot and shutdown there. A three-way merge of the two versions of the test has no textual conflict, but the merged loop also runs logout, which makes one attempt. A sandboxed run of the merged test, with the logout mode restored, fails on the logout case. Whichever PR lands second would need a per-action expected count. #12575 and #7216 also add an `omarchy-osd` stub and conflict textually in this file. #13076 conflicts in the same file and schedules shutdown without `--on-active=2s`, so if it lands first, logout would no longer use the same flags as shutdown.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Follow-up source review of `0056062e` against the earlier head `9c497363`, base `9c5482c` and `quattro` tip `3faafba`, including `bin/omarchy` command discovery, the test runner and the omarchy PKGBUILDs. The power test, dispatcher help commands and trial merges with the `quattro` tip and with #11151 ran in an isolated sandbox with all backends stubbed. No real logout or dev-linked session was tested. The #12233 link was read from the GitHub API.
